title: USB-C port, flush in a wall
summary: The board's USB-C socket sits in a close-fitting pocket in the wall, walled in on all sides with its face level with the outside, so the cable seats the way it does on a laptop. The board's end tucks into a shallow relief in the wall's inner face so the socket can reach the outside.

views.label: In the wall
views.caption: Turn it to the outside: the socket's face is flush, with a 0.15 gap all round. Inside, the board's end sits in a relief, leaving 1.5 of wall round the socket. Slide the socket out to see the pocket.

views.label: Fit piece
views.caption: Four pockets, 0.10 to 0.30 per side, marked with 1 to 4 dots. Set up for the FireBeetle; the C3 Super Mini fits the same relief.

specs.title: The pocket
specs.note: If a socket overhangs less than 1.0 (the S3's 0.38), its face sits back from the outside by the difference rather than leave a thin wall.
specs.badgeNote: the gap is set by the fit piece

checks: Slide the board's socket in from behind: light push, no rattle?
Is the face flush with the outside?
Plug a cable in from the front: does it seat fully and click?
Does the gap round the socket look even?
fit.print: Print base down, no supports, in the enclosure's material.
